extracted.intended_audience: criminal judges, jurists, trial lawyers, and other legal professionals involved in evidence-taking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for judges (criminalists) on applying psychological principles and a scientific method to the taking, testing, and evaluation of evidence and witness testimony at trial. Emphasizes methods to elicit reliable testimony, assess evidence value, and manage participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part methodological program
rubrics_metrics.description: Our method will be that fundamental to all psychological investigation, and may be divided into three parts: 1. The preparation of a review of psychological phenomena. 2. Study of causal relationships. 3. Establishment of the principles of psychic activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the discipline systematically: first collect and describe phenomena, then seek causal relations, then formulate general principles applicable to criminal procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Socratic method to correct witness error
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead the witness, as Socrates did the slave, to discover and state the truth rather than simply accepting his spontaneous assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek to correct a witness’s false conceptions by questioning that enables the witness to find his own error, avoiding intimidation or coercion that merely produces acquiescence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding suggestion and not over-leading the witness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pervert the witness from possibly sound opinions by excessive leading; distinguish legitimate openness to conviction from suggestive questioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to introduce answers or conclusions via questioning; correct gently and allow the witness to come to truth without being unduly suggestible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the subject and real issue precisely before inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fundamental investigation must first of all establish the nature of its subject matter; witnesses and judges must know exactly what is to be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the issue under investigation is clearly formulated so that both questioning and testimony address the same thing, avoiding mutual misunderstanding (the judge and witness speaking of different matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the natural-science method: constantify, isolate, vary conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The method consists in keeping constant necessary conditions, isolating elements, varying them in a numerical order, and observing changes in the effect, i.e., from facts to ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare present case conditions with others (standardize), abstract individual elements of evidence, vary assumptions about them, and observe how the overall proof is affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of evidence along two axes: reliability and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The valuation must be made in respect of (1) its reliability (subjective and relative), and (2) its significance (objective and absolute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a testimony ask (a) was the witness able and willing to speak the truth, and (b) what influence can this evidence, if reliable, exercise on the organization and outcome of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical variation test for evidence (consider lie, error, inference)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each statement suppose it might be a lie, incorrect observation, false inference, etc., and ask whether the proof of guilt (the effect) still remains just under these variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this counterfactual variation to determine whether conviction is justified under alternative possibilities; convict only if the accusation holds under reasonable variations you can account for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine order of succession (temporal and causal order) rigorously
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of the order of succession is most important; oversight of order is the largest cause of failures in evidence determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine temporal and causal sequences carefully—many impossibilities or mistakes are discovered only by scrutinizing the order in which events or impressions occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize and compare with similar cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardization consists in comparing the conditions of the present instance with those of other cases whenever similar circumstances are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analogy and comparison to help determine whether certain instruments of evidence or conditions typically lead to the same effect (proof) in other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate individual sources of evidence and determine their individual values
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract individual statements, visual impressions, or effects and determine their value separately before integrating them into the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze each piece of evidence on its own terms (e.g., witness testimony, examination of premises, obduction, protocol) and quantify or comparatively evaluate their contribution to the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not merely allow witnesses to say what they choose; actively elicit fullest evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge's dereliction is to throw the witness the question and permit him to say what he chooses—this leaves part of the untruthful or suppressed matter to the witness and the larger part to the judge's failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judge must work to bring out the utmost value of evidence, both for and against the prisoner, by guiding testimony rather than passively accepting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train witnesses to want to tell the truth and to be able to tell it
rubrics_metrics.description: This training must in each case take two directions: it must make him want to tell the truth; it must make him able to tell the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the witness’s conscientiousness and provide questioning that helps him structure and report memories accurately (especially for laypersons unaccustomed to testifying).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage courtroom psychology to produce interest and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: The psychological handling of participants (presiding justice, jurymen, experts) affects their conscientiousness and performance; the judge must lead and train them anew to interest, conscientiousness and co-operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge’s manner and demonstrated interest can motivate experts and participants to apply themselves fully; conversely indifference can depress performance—so actively manage group dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between exposing errors and avoiding making truthful witnesses vacillate
rubrics_metrics.description: It is difficult to correct apparent false conceptions without going too far and causing a witness who is otherwise telling the truth to become vacillating and doubtful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questioning should be cautious: avoid aggressive attacks that unduly shake conscientious witnesses, but persist enough to reveal genuine mistakes or falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preconceptions—work from facts to ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The contemporary scientific direction requires 'from facts to ideas'—observe facts without prejudice or maxims built on preconceptions; then theorize modestly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist imposing legal or theoretical preconceptions on raw testimony; let evidence be collected and purified first, then draw inferences conservatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess witness character and situational conditions affecting testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering testimony, determine the appraisement of the person who presents it and the conditions under which he is important (e.g., excitement of court, authority's influence, age, sex, cultivation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate personal reliability factors (temperament, honesty, habitual vagueness) and situational influences (courtroom excitement, authority pressure) when judging the weight of testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical observation and practiced knowledge of human nature over book-learning alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of human nature is acquired only by persevering observation, comparison, summarization, and further comparison; books alone give little usable skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop practical expertise through repeated real-world contact with witnesses, liars, experts, and different social types rather than relying solely on theoretical texts.
